channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [DW] Gerhard Schröder visits latest Russian employer, Hyperglobus
item.description: Former German Chancellor Gerhard Schröder visited a Moscow supermarket in his new role on the supervisory board. Schröder is no stranger to retirement stipends in Russia — or the scandal that accompanies them.

item.title: [DW] EU enlargement: European Commission tables reforms to prepare bloc for new members
item.description: The European Commission is proposing earlier access to EU markets for candidate countries, new voting rules to reduce vetoes and extra safeguards for a bigger bloc. But is the reform fair — or even feasible?

item.title: [DW] Suspected pneumonic plague in Siberia: What we know about the disease
item.description: After a worker at a Russian plague research institute in Siberia died October 2, 2026, nearly 200 of her contacts were under medical observation. But authorities there denied pneumonic plague had caused the death.

item.title: [DW] Where is Spain headed after the snap election announcement?
item.description: Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez is taking a gamble by calling an early election in Spain. The housing crisis, migration and the rise of the right-wing populist Vox party are all likely to dominate the campaign.

item.title: [Politico Europe] EU, Canada and Lithuania pull out of disinformation conference after US pressure
item.description: The Trump administration was bothered by panels that referred to the U.S. as a disinformation threat.

item.title: [Financial Times] Trump considers ‘terminating’ campaign advisers after Balkans trip
item.description: President says Chris LaCivita and James Blair guiding pro-Russian government less than a month before midterms could be a ‘conflict’

item.title: [Politico Europe] French PM tries to defuse anger over schools, fuel and agriculture in sweeping speech
item.description: With students protesting and fuel prices adding to pressure on households, Lecornu pledged new measures to address France’s mounting polycrisis.

item.title: [Financial Times] The online life of the Flydubai attacker
item.description: Co-pilot of flight 1073 gravitated towards the ‘manosphere’ and expressed misogynistic views

item.title: [EU Observer] Broken promise of ‘European solution’ on migration overshadows next week’s summit
item.description: EU leaders have run out of ideas as they keep rehashing the same solutions on migration.

item.title: [Politico Europe] EU Parliament defends secret ballots that kept far right out of top committee jobs
item.description: Patriots group takes Parliament to court, saying it was excluded from key posts.

item.title: [EU Observer] If it worked with Ukraine, why not also Iran? Green MEPs urge EU to tax oil super profits
item.description: As Europeans foot the bill for the Iran war while oil firms' profits surge, the EU Parliament's left hit a commission-shaped brick wall in Strasbourg.

item.title: [EU Observer] Drone strikes on Black Sea cargo ships point to wider European arc of Russia hybrid threats
item.description: Drone attacks on commercial ships in the Black Sea point to a 360-degree threat of Russian hybrid attacks, covering also the EU's southern and eastern flanks.

item.title: [EU Observer] Ukraine forces becoming more agile under new commander-in-chief Drapatyi, who is also drafting a ‘grand strategy’ for the war (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,686)
item.description: Anonymous commanders paint a picture of an army suddenly trusted to improvise, led by rehabilitated critics and 30‑something officers, while Russia marks Putin’s birthday with mass strikes and a burning oil tanker off Sochi’s coast.

item.title: [EU Observer] After 50 EU summits, leaders are still copy‑pasting failed migration ‘solutions’
item.description: A trawl through 52 sets of summit conclusions reveals how EU leaders keep quietly copy‑pasting calls for tougher returns and externalised border control, while largely sidelining legal migration and resettlement schemes that could save lives.

item.title: [EU Observer] Sanctions in February, handshakes in September: EU’s flip-flop Iran policy is putting lives at risk
item.description: By sitting down with senior Iranian figures who publicly back the Revolutionary Guard while keeping sanctions limited to technocratic lists, EU governments risk undermining their own leverage at a time of rising regional tensions.

item.title: [EU Observer] Why Oxygen Forensics US tech CEO selling software to Europe agencies was arrested
item.description: US authorities arrested men who sold a forensic software to government bodies across Europe, hid the tool's true owners and concealed its Russian development.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU will need to tax AI ‘workers’ to keep funding human pensions
item.description: As AI shifts work from people to machines, it will force a rethink of who gets taxed, on what, and where. Nowhere is that question more urgent than in Europe, which funds the world's most comprehensive welfare states primarily through taxes on work.

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: Are we now heading to a trade war with China?
item.description: Chinese carmakers are gaining more space in the European market, provoking EU debates about competitiveness.

item.title: [DW] EU seeks ways to make expansion more palatable to members
item.description: The European Commission has put forward ideas it hopes will both ease the EU expansion process and allay concerns among existing members. Several countries, not least war-torn Ukraine, are among the candidates.

item.title: [DW] France's conundrum: How to cut spending amid protests
item.description: Prime Minister Lecornu is pledging to improve schools at a time when the government seeks to save billions. France's dilemma can be seen across the EU: How to cut spending when citizens are demanding more from the state?

item.title: [DW] Fact check: Misleading claims spark plague fears in Russia
item.description: The death of a lab worker at a plague research institute in Russia has sparked claims about a lab accident, hundreds of infections and international spread. Some of these viral narratives are misleading.

item.title: [DW] Security in the Black Sea region: is Bulgaria the weak link in Europe's defense against threats from Russia?
item.description: Two ships have sunk off the coast of Bulgaria and Romania after drone attacks in recent days. Sofia has held back on pointing the finger at Russia. What does that mean for security in the Black Sea and the region?

item.title: [DW] South Korea recalls Ukraine ambassador amid POW dispute
item.description: South Korea has said it will recall its ambassador to Ukraine. Seoul is upset about a transfer of North Korean prisoners of war being made public knowledge at the UN and had demanded — but not received — an apology.

item.title: [DW] As Russia steps up attacks on Ukrainian data centers, could Ukraine soon be offline?
item.description: As Russia targets Ukraine's data centers more and more, experts say the country's internet system is too robust to shut down entirely. However, services could become more expensive.

item.title: [DW] Middle Corridor: Can Bulgaria be a safe gateway for Asian imports to the EU?
item.description: The EU wants more trade via the Middle Corridor, which could bring big benefits for Bulgaria. But Tuesday's drone attacks on commercial ships off the Bulgarian coast are a stark reminder of the security risks involved.

item.title: [Financial Times] Oil prices jump on tanker attack and slowing flows through Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Transit through vital waterway rose close to 90% of prewar levels last month but has since fallen sharply

item.title: [Financial Times] Houthi attacks on Saudi airports kill three people
item.description: Strikes are latest escalation in conflict between Saudi Arabia and Iran-backed militants in Yemen

item.title: [EU Observer] French school protests to continue, after prime minister ignores demands
item.description: Two-weeks long protests by French high-school students demanding better education conditions risk getting more heated due the French government's lack of response.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU disowns Vilnius event that warned of US political interference, but France maintains support
item.description: US pressure pushed some European governments to disown a Vilnius conference on disinformation and interference, which had dared to ask if America itself was now warping European politics.

item.title: [Financial Times] Germany’s ex-spymaster admits holding files but denies treason
item.description: August Hanning’s lawyer says his client was ‘in possession’ of confidential documents but never paid for them or passed them on to foreign powers

item.title: [EU Observer] Morocco’s surveillance state does not stop at Western Sahara — and Europe can no longer pretend not to know
item.description: As new evidence emerges of Moroccan spying on Sahrawi activists, including in Europe, European governments continue to deepen their security ties with Rabat without seriously questioning how those capabilities are being used.

item.title: [Politico Europe] UK and Israel broker compromise over East Jerusalem consulate
item.description: Both sides claim a win — but relations have soured over British plans to sanction West Bank settlements.

item.title: [EU Observer] Cut the EU budget and we all lose
item.description: As national leaders call for massive cuts in the next EU budget, the parliament’s budget chiefs, MEP Siegfried Mureşan and Carla Tavares, warn that slashing EU cash now will undercut Europe’s competitiveness, security and social safety net for years to come.

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: Are student protests in France actually being fuelled by Mélenchon’s party LFI?
item.description: Production: By Europod, in co-production with Sphera Network. item.title: [Politico Europe] Will Berlin help Britain rejoin the EU?
item.description: With conference season in the rear-view mirror, Andy Burnham jets off to Germany for his first European trip as PM – but how much do Anglo-German relations matter right now? Sam Coates and Anne McElvoy look ahead to his meeting with German chancellor Friedrich Merz as the countries attempt to align ambitions and maybe find […]

item.title: [EU Observer] Germany’s most promising industries depend on China, clashing with Berlin’s derisking push, study finds
item.description: Small electrical firms best placed to drive Germany's industrial renewal rely on China as their main supplier, competitor and sometimes customer, leaving Berlin with a dilemma: the fastest way to scale them up is with the very Chinese components it wants to reduce reliance on.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Can Europe finally get tough on China?
item.description: Trade Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič is kicking off his visit to China today — and the stakes are high. On today’s show, Zoya Sheftalovich and Sarah Wheaton discuss the most important topic on the agenda: Europe’s trade deficit with China. France and Germany are finally on the same page and want Brussels to get tougher on […]

item.title: [Financial Times] French bond sell-off prompts ‘bottom fishing’ across Europe
item.description: Fears of a blow-up similar to the Eurozone debt crisis have been overdone, asset managers say

item.title: [Financial Times] Real men don’t do climate change
item.description: Research on the gender differences in how people think about global warming suggests campaigns and communications may need a rethink

item.title: [Financial Times] How a trillion-dollar hedge fund borrowing spree became Wall Street’s cash cow
item.description: Banks’ trading businesses are booming, but post-crisis regulation means it is no longer them placing the bets

item.title: [Politico Europe] Hat Merz seine CDU noch im Griff?
item.description: Die Brandmauer bröckelt weiter und bringt Friedrich Merz in Bedrängnis. Nach der Wahl von Tobias Rausch von der AfD zum Landtagspräsidenten in Sachsen-Anhalt womöglich mit CDU-Stimmen wächst die parteiinterne Nervosität. Rasmus Buchsteiner analysiert, warum der CDU-Chef die Kontrolle über die Debatte verliert und wie SPD-Verteidigungsminister Boris Pistorius die Situation mit seinem historischen Vergleich anheizt. Außenpolitisch […]

item.title: [Politico Europe] Far-right surge threatens Europe’s drive to rearm
item.description: Insurgent far-right parties are seizing on cost-of-living grievances and waning support for defense spending.

item.title: [Politico Europe] How Polanski has tried to sell himself in Holborn and St Pancras
item.description: Analysis of the online air war shows the Green leader pitching himself as a safe protest vote for Labour switchers in the London seat.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Far-right Vox sees election as its big chance to reshape Spain
item.description: The party is a strong position to push for ministerial jobs in a right-wing coalition.

item.title: [Financial Times] China races to build data centres in bid for AI supremacy
item.description: Beijing is rolling out computing infrastructure at breakneck speed in Inner Mongolia

item.title: [DW] Nationalists top Bosnia-Herzegovina's divisive election
item.description: Bosnia-Herzegovina's three-member presidency is set to be dominated by nationalists from the three major ethnic groups, including Zeljka ​Cvijanovic, backed by disqualified Serb secessionist leader Milorad Dodik.

item.title: [DW] Merz, Macron seek tougher EU measures against unfair trade
item.description: Emmanuel Macron and Friedrich Merz have written to Ursula von der Leyen, calling for tougher EU mechanisms against unfair trade practices by other states. They name no names but seem to have China or the US in mind.

item.title: [DW] Bosnia election: New steps to prevent electoral fraud, but nationalist parties remain on top
item.description: New technology has stopped votes being cast on behalf of dead or absent voters, and turnout has fallen to a record low. But it was a case of deja vu in Bosnia's elections with the same parties winning.

item.title: [DW] Hundreds of French schools shut, teen loses hand in protests
item.description: The student protests that rocked France last week have prompted authorities to keep up to 500 schools closed on Monday. A teenage boy lost his hand, seemingly while trying to pick up a police tear gas grenade.
